arguments.command:
python -c "
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

# Two timezones with same offset but different names
tz1 = timezone(timedelta(hours=1), name='+01:00')
tz2 = timezone(timedelta(hours=1), name='+0100')

dt1 = datetime(1997, 7, 16, 19, 20, tzinfo=tz1)
dt2 = datetime(1997, 7, 16, 19, 20, tzinfo=tz2)

print('dt1:', dt1)
print('dt2:', dt2)
print('dt1 == dt2:', dt1 == dt2)
print('dt1.utctimetuple():', dt1.utctimetuple())
print('dt2.utctimetuple():', dt2.utctimetuple())
"

Aha! So the test actually compares datetime objects, not just tzinfo. And when comparing two datetime objects with different timezone info (but same offset), Python's datetime comparison should work correctly because it normalizes to UTC for comparison.
